nfl.oneThing: Lions star Aidan Hutchinson is out for the season with a torn ACL in his right knee, sources told NFL Network, and Detroit (7-2) now has to get through the rest of the year without him.

headlines.title: Hutchinson out for the season with a torn ACL
headlines.summary: Lions star Aidan Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season after tests showed a torn ACL in his right knee, sources told NFL Network. Detroit is 7-2 and the NFC's No. 2 seed, sitting behind the 8-1 49ers. The Lions have been one of the league's better teams this year, so the loss of a star this late in the season is a serious blow.
headlines.whyItMatters: Detroit is in good playoff position, so the rest of the roster now has to carry the load through the back half of the season.

headlines.title: Burrow's MVP case is built on the passing numbers
headlines.summary: Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns in Cincinnati's 38–18 win over the Steelers, completing 35 of 44 passes. He has 20 touchdown passes during the Bengals' five-game winning streak. Across the season he leads the league with 27 touchdown passes and has 2,795 passing yards, second to Jordan Love's 2,838.
headlines.whyItMatters: Cincinnati is 7-2 and the AFC's No. 4 seed, so his numbers are coming from a team that is firmly in the playoff picture.

headlines.title: Dolphins' defensive line thins out, and Gonzalez is cut
headlines.summary: Miami will be without defensive tackle Zeek Biggers for the rest of the season after knee surgery to repair a torn lateral meniscus. He was hurt in Week 10 against the Colts. The week before, Zach Sieler ruptured a biceps, and Jordan Phillips hurt his arm in the same loss. Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr. are the only healthy defensive tackles on the 53-man roster. Miami also waived kicker Zane Gonzalez a day after he missed two field goals and an extra point in a 24–22 loss to Indianapolis.
headlines.whyItMatters: Miami is 1-8 and 14th in the AFC, so the focus is on recovery. The hope is that Biggers recovers fully ahead of the 2027 season.

headlines.title: Steelers turn to the Eagles after 38–18 loss
headlines.summary: Pittsburgh lost 38–18 at Cincinnati on Sunday night, a loss of 20 points. Coach Mike McCarthy wants the defeat to be one game and nothing more. The Steelers (6-3) face the Eagles next Sunday, a cross-state rival in a city where Pittsburgh hasn't won a regular-season game since 1965. Philadelphia is 2-7 and has lost seven straight.

headlines.title: Rams lose Shelton for four to six weeks
headlines.summary: Centre Coleman Shelton strained his hamstring against the Cardinals and will miss four to six weeks, the team said. Dylan McMahon partially tore his patellar tendon and goes on injured reserve, so Beaux Limmer moved to centre. The Rams are also without receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, plus Terrance Ferguson and Steve Avila.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Rams are 6-4 after four straight wins. They're on their bye this week before hosting Green Bay in Week 12, and their offensive line depth is now being tested.

teamNews.title: Mendoza shows poise in first start, but Raiders lose 21–13
teamNews.text: Fernando Mendoza made his first career start in a 21–13 loss to the Seahawks. Coach Klint Kubiak said he 'showed poise', and Mendoza scored in the game. The Raiders led at halftime but had no answer in the second half.

teamNews.title: Bowers day-to-day with an ankle injury
teamNews.text: Kubiak said Monday that Brock Bowers is day-to-day after leaving Sunday's game. He called the injury 'not as bad as we thought'. Bowers is listed as questionable for the next game.

teamNews.title: Practice squad moves and a new quarterback
teamNews.text: The Raiders signed QB Brett Rypien to the practice squad and released DE Bralen Trice from it. Yahoo Sports also reports the Raiders have signed a former Buccaneers quarterback.

teamNews.title: Raiders (4-6) head to Denver next
teamNews.text: The Raiders are 4-6 and 10th in the AFC, two games behind the last playoff spot. They play at the Broncos (7-2) next week.

nba.oneThing: San Antonio's 12-game winning streak has them 12-2 and first in the West, and the Spurs have moved to No. 1 in the power rankings.

headlines.title: Spurs stretch winning streak to 12
headlines.summary: The Spurs beat the Jazz 110–102 to make it 12 straight wins, and Utah's 12th straight loss. San Antonio is 12-2, level with the Lakers on record but first in the West on the standings. The streak has come with depth, with Victor Wembanyama, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper all shining in the last week. The Spurs now sit at No. 1 in the power rankings.
headlines.whyItMatters: Their 12-2 start puts them out front in the West while the streak keeps building. Detroit is next, and it's a big test.

headlines.title: Embiid's season-high 37 leads 76ers past Nets without LeBron
headlines.summary: Joel Embiid scored a season-high 37 and Jaylen Brown added 31 as Philadelphia beat Brooklyn 135–123. Julius Randle had 33 for the Nets, and Nolan Traore matched his career high with 23. Philadelphia is 4-0 without LeBron James. Brown had a scare after a fourth-quarter collision with Randle left him bleeding. He returned with a bandage but wasn't in the game for the finish.
headlines.whyItMatters: Philadelphia (12-3) leads the East, and its 4-0 record without James shows its depth is holding up.

headlines.title: Magic beat Celtics 115–105 for fourth straight win
headlines.summary: Orlando rallied in the fourth quarter to beat Boston 115–105. Desmond Bane had 24 points and eight rebounds, and Franz Wagner added 21 points and nine assists. The Magic shot 41 of 82 from the field and earned their first win in Boston since December 2022. It was Boston's first home loss of the season, ending a six-game winning streak.
headlines.whyItMatters: Orlando moves to 6-7 and into the East's No. 8 seed. Boston (11-3) remains second in the East.

headlines.title: Heat keep rolling behind Giannis, but Adebayo leaves early
headlines.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo had 20 points and 13 rebounds as Miami beat Houston 128–110 for a fifth straight win. Andrew Wiggins and Klay Thompson each scored 17, and the Heat never trailed. Bam Adebayo left with hip tightness after 16 first-half minutes. Coach Erik Spoelstra said it was a precaution and the injury isn't expected to be a long-term issue.
headlines.whyItMatters: Miami is 8-6 and fourth in the East, and it's been strong without its anchor on defence.

headlines.title: Mitchell's 39 sends Cavaliers past Bulls, Mobley out again
headlines.summary: Donovan Mitchell scored 39 as Cleveland beat Chicago 126–115. Jarrett Allen had 13 points and 14 rebounds. Evan Mobley is out again with a sprained right toe and will miss at least another seven to 10 days, after first hurting it in a win over the Knicks.
headlines.whyItMatters: Cleveland is 8-7 and seventh in the East, so Allen and the wings need to cover for Mobley while he's out.

headlines.title: Boozer's 29 helps Grizzlies hand Wizards eighth straight loss
headlines.summary: Memphis rookie Cameron Boozer scored a season-high 29 in a 136–120 win at Washington, and the Grizzlies rallied from 12 points down. Zach Edey had 23 points and 10 rebounds. The Wizards (4-11) have lost eight straight, and the matchup included No. 1 draft pick AJ Dybantsa.
headlines.whyItMatters: Washington is 12th in the East. Memphis (10-4) is fifth in the West.

recaps.text: Golden State was without Stephen Curry, who was ruled out with an abdominal injury, and New Orleans made the most of it. Jeremiah Fears ran the offence with 10 assists, and the upset is one of the bigger results of the night. Yaxel Lendeborg's 28 points weren't enough to pull the Warriors back.

recaps.keyLine: Embiid 37 pts, 5 reb, 1 ast · Brown 31 pts, 13 reb, 4 ast · Randle 33 pts, 6 reb, 1 ast · Porter Jr. 25 pts, 6 reb, 2 ast
recaps.text: Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown carried the 76ers in Brooklyn, where LeBron James sat out the second half of a back-to-back. Brown's game was briefly interrupted after a head collision with Julius Randle left both players bleeding. Randle's 33 kept Brooklyn in it, but Embiid scored six straight late to push the lead back out.

recaps.keyLine: Bane 24 pts, 8 reb, 5 ast · Wagner 21 pts, 8 reb, 9 ast · Tatum 24 pts, 12 reb, 4 ast · George 22 pts, 8 reb, 3 ast, 5 3PM
recaps.text: Orlando rallied in the fourth quarter to beat Boston, which had been one of the East's strongest teams. Jayson Tatum had 24 points and 12 rebounds, but also five of Boston's 11 turnovers. The Magic shot 50 per cent from the field, and Desmond Bane and Franz Wagner made the difference late.

recaps.keyLine: Towns 28 pts, 17 reb, 3 ast · Brunson 28 pts, 1 reb, 9 ast · Barnes 30 pts, 9 reb, 4 ast · Shead 19 pts, 2 reb, 4 ast
recaps.text: Karl-Anthony Towns had 28 points and 17 rebounds, and Jalen Brunson added 28 as the Knicks outlasted Toronto 112–108 in overtime. Scottie Barnes scored 30 in defeat, and Immanuel Quickley had 17 points. The result was tight in the last minutes, and it went to overtime.

contextCard.title: How Player of the Week works
contextCard.body: The NBA names a Player of the Week in each conference, based on the previous week's games. It's a weekly award, so a win doesn't mean a player has had the best season. It's a good way to spot who's been carrying a team through a busy stretch.
